correctness.rationale: Both component proximal maps are strict contractions. The exact invariant first and centered second moments give the stationary risk. SymPy verifies the derivative equals a positive rational factor times the increasing quadratic Pκ(p); Pκ(0)<0 and Pκ(1)=-2κ(κ+2)(κ²-2κ-7), giving the unique global interior/endpoint frontier κ=1+2√2. Unbiased-risk and objective limits follow from exact substitutions. Reproducible symbolic and 450 exact finite-time recurrence/path checks support, but do not replace, the infinite-horizon proof. No probabilistic finite enumeration is misrepresented as exhaustive.

value.rationale: A natural steady-state stochastic-resolvent design problem has a complete exact probability classification, including a nontrivial interior-to-endpoint switch, proof of unique minimizers, and the mathematical distinction between mean-unbiased sampling and minimum terminal squared loss. The asymptotically unbounded risk ratio and nonzero unbiased-sampler objective gap show a substantive, not solely numerical, difference. Scope is explicitly limited to uncorrected two-component scalar quadratics, so the result is a motivated benchmark rather than a claim of optimal general learning.
